text:
T.J. Hughes was never drafted. He scored 57 points in 40 games for Michigan last season, signed with Colorado as a free agent, and has played every one of his 24 NHL games for a team that needed bodies who could make plays. He's averaging about 15 minutes a night and has 13 points, six of them on the power play.

The goal total is the odd number. Hughes has two goals on 6.4 expected, the quality of his chances, so he's shooting under 4% on 54 shots. He keeps getting to good spots, and goals tend to follow chances. Of everything on his line, that's the most likely to change.

The five-on-five picture is more mixed. Colorado wins the shot attempts with him on the ice but trails slightly on chance quality, and the team does better at even strength when he sits. That's normal for a rookie still finding his game. With Nathan MacKinnon out (reported at 12 weeks), there's room in this lineup for a forward who can produce. Watch whether his minutes grow, and whether the shots start going in.
headline: Hughes keeps getting looks that won't go in
